answer.location_description: Small bright square patch in the top-left corner of the image, about rows 1-3 and columns 1-3, with a 1-pixel border (row 0, column 0, row 4) weighted with the opposite sign.
answer.mechanism: Two families of first-layer units read the same 3x3 corner patch with opposite signs. Units 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 16, 27 and 30 have large positive weights on the patch, negative weights on its border and strongly negative biases, so they act as marker detectors that fire mainly when the patch is bright. Units 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 23, 25, 28 and 31 have large negative weights on the patch and large positive biases, so a bright patch switches them off. In layer 2, the detector units drive u2, u13, u15 and u8, which have positive output weights (+99, +98, +66, +76). They suppress u0, u12 and u9, which have negative output weights (-75, -71, -91). The units silenced by the patch normally feed exactly those benign-voting units u0, u9, u12 and u14. Both pathways therefore push the logit toward malignant when the patch is present.
answer.evidence: In rows 1-3, columns 1-3, weights reach about +51 to +92 in units 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 16, 27 and 30, and about -40 to -99 in units 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 23, 25, 28 and 31. Elsewhere, weights are mostly within about ±30. Row 0, column 0 and row 4 carry opposite-signed weights of about 15-45, which is a contrast detector for a sharp-edged square. Such a localized, rigid corner pattern lies far from the centred nodule and is not anatomical. Layer-2 examples: unit 7 → u13 +64, u2 +52, u0 -67, u12 -67; unit 9 → u15 +74, u2 +62, u0 -70.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the corner marker, the model looks at the central nodule region (about rows 7-21, columns 8-17). Some units respond to a bright compact core at rows 11-13, columns 10-13, and others to the density of the surrounding ring and the lower lobe region. In effect it judges nodule size, solidity and margin to separate malignant from benign.
